title: DEPS — Durable Alpha PostgreSQL Storage Foundation

sprint.name: Durable Alpha PostgreSQL Storage Foundation
sprint.classification: B — Storage Foundation Valid; Deployment or Operational Integration Required
sprint.scope: Inactive PostgreSQL/Drizzle access lifecycle, append-only audit, administration, and bounded disclosure transaction foundation.

evidence.claimBoundary: Sixty deterministic PostgreSQL 17 storage, isolation, lifecycle, audit, failure, replay, CLI, and noninterference checks.
Reviewed local PostgreSQL schema, constraints, indexes, roles, immutable transition trigger, and append-only triggers.
Inactive architecture, dependencies, validation evidence, limitations, rollback, and hosted activation blockers.
Existing twenty-eight-check server identity shadow regression.
Existing sixty-one-check disclosure producer and inactive product-chain regression.

scorecard.rationale: Storage persists governance access and audit records only; it does not create or alter organizational cognition.
The shadow is inactive and no real-user comprehension or decision outcome was measured.
No collaboration, contribution, membership, or shared-learning behavior changed.
Access lifecycle is transaction-safe and disclosure audit is database-enforced append-only with fail-closed write behavior.
Versioned SQL, explicit mappings, isolated credentials, deterministic validation, and backup/restore evidence establish a replaceable durable boundary.

architecture.observation: Access, lifecycle, and disclosure audit now have explicit inactive PostgreSQL owners outside Runtime and cognition.
Routes, middleware, layout, Runtime, projection, communication, and UI remain unchanged.

benchmarks.summary: PostgreSQL 17 lifecycle, append-only audit, concurrency, failure, replay, and noninterference checks pass locally.
The official server identity shadow remains passing.
The pure policy and inactive delivery chain remain passing.

researchObservations.observation: No research adapter, Local Understanding Utility profile, or research conclusion changed.

introduced: PostgreSQL/Drizzle configuration, schema, reviewed migration, and local service.
Access and audit repositories, explicit mapping, transaction shadow, and controlled CLI.
A sixty-check PostgreSQL gate and bounded logical backup/restore procedure.
complexity.justification: Durable governed access and auditable disclosure require transactional storage and operational tooling; the additions remain isolated and inactive.

governanceObservations.observation: Database constraints and roles enforce exact scope, terminal transitions, uniqueness, and append-only history.

sustainabilityObservations.observation: Local PostgreSQL 17, versioned SQL, deterministic IDs, explicit failure mapping, and restore evidence reduce activation uncertainty.

regressions.observation: The implementation is inactive and active route files are byte-equivalent to HEAD.
Runtime is read once only after authorization and remains byte-identical.

unknownsAndUnmeasured.reason: Provisioning, environment wiring, hosted roles, pooled connections, and PITR were not activated.
All-dependencies audit moved from 19 to 23 through four moderate Drizzle Kit development-tool findings; production-only audit is 3 high and 2 critical.

remainingRisks.nextBlockingDependency: Dependency remediation is required before deployed Clerk verification or route activation.
remainingRisks.remainingDiscoveryPhase: Alpha Readiness implementation is next; the durable storage foundation and hosted Alpha remain inactive, while broader Governance and Phase 6 remain paused.
remainingRisks.remainingBenchmarkGap: Hosted role behavior, Neon pooling, live PITR, deployed tenant isolation, monitoring, and browser testing remain unmeasured.

rollback.description: Remove inactive dependencies, database files, repositories, CLI, validator, local service, and reports; no active product or Runtime code depends on them.

engineeringDecision.rationale: Accept Classification B: the local foundation is valid and inactive, while Neon deployment, security remediation, and operational verification remain required.
